overview.title: Study Manager
overview.purpose: Many students struggle to manage their study time and to understand how their study habits relate to academic performance. Study Manager lets students log study hours per course, log quiz and exam grades, view statistics about their habits, and get a predicted score for an upcoming quiz or exam based on how many hours they have studied.
overview.intendedUsers: Students who want to track their study hours and understand how those hours relate to their quiz and exam results.
overview.scopeNote: Two-person team: the base scope in this plan is sufficient. The instructions favor a smaller application that works reliably over an ambitious one with incomplete features, so anything marked "stretch" is cut first if time runs short.

userFeatures.feature: Log how many hours they studied for a course (date, course, hours, optional note).
Track study time per course: table of sessions filterable by course, totals per course and per week.
Log quiz and exam grades (date, course, type, name, score 0-100).
View statistics: total hours, number of sessions, average session length, average score per course, hours-vs-score correlation, charts.
View a predicted score for an upcoming quiz or exam from the number of hours studied, with the regression statistics behind it.
Load sample data with one click so the grader can see personalized predictions immediately.

column.name: study_hours
column.description: Total hours spent studying for the exam

notes.note: Synthetic data: generated in R as grade = 40 + 5 * study_hours + Normal(0, 10), clipped to 0-100. State this in the README.
The data card says hours range 0-12, but the column histogram shows 0-10. Read the real min and max from the file at runtime; never hard-code the range.
Include the file in data/ (MIT license allows it) and give the Kaggle URL in the README as a backup.

dataSources.dataSource: About 30 sessions and 8-10 graded assessments across 2 courses, so that at least one course has enough points for a per-course regression.

derivedData.name: hours_per_assessment
derivedData.definition: For each graded assessment, hours = the sum of that course's study sessions dated after the previous assessment of the same course and on or before this assessment's date. This matches the Kaggle meaning of study_hours (total hours for one exam).
derivedData.implementation: pd.merge_asof(sessions sorted by date, grades sorted by date, on="date", by="course", direction="forward") assigns each session to the next assessment of its course; then groupby the assessment and sum hours. Sessions after the last assessment are unassigned and become "hours so far" for the upcoming assessment, which pre-fills the Prediction tab.

exception.name: StudyManagerError
exception.description: Base class for the app's errors

errorCondition.trigger: Negative or zero hours, more than 24 hours, a score outside 0-100, an empty course name, or a future date.
errorCondition.response: st.warning with the exact problem; nothing is saved; the form keeps its values.

errorCondition.trigger: A user CSV is missing, empty, unparseable (pandas.errors.ParserError, EmptyDataError), or missing required columns.
errorCondition.response: A missing user file is created with headers. A corrupt file shows st.error and the app continues with empty data instead of crashing.
st.error with download instructions; logging and statistics still work; only the Prediction tab is disabled.

errorCondition.trigger: Fewer than 5 graded assessments, or all assessments have identical hours.
errorCondition.response: Fall back to the next model tier and show which model was used.

errorCondition.trigger: Malformed rows: non-numeric hours or scores, invalid dates.
errorCondition.response: pd.to_numeric and pd.to_datetime with errors="coerce", drop the bad rows, and show how many were skipped.

errorCondition.trigger: Requested hours are outside the baseline data range, or the raw prediction exceeds 100.
errorCondition.response: np.clip to 0-100 and add a warning that the prediction is an extrapolation.

dataProcessing.operation: read_csv with column checks; to_datetime and to_numeric with errors="coerce"; dropna to remove malformed rows.
groupby("course").agg(total=sum, sessions=count, mean_length=mean) for per-course statistics.
pd.Grouper(key="date", freq="W") for weekly study totals.
merge_asof by course to attach sessions to assessments, then groupby and sum (hours_per_assessment).
Series.corr between hours and scores; mean score per course.
np.clip for score bounds; np.linspace for regression lines; vectorized predictions over arrays of hours.

advancedComponent.whyMeaningful: The regression is the core of feature F5, not a decoration: it produces the prediction, decides which model to trust, and reports how reliable that model is.

modelTiers.tier: Fit on the user's hours_per_assessment for the selected course when it has 5 or more points.
Otherwise fit on all of the user's assessments across courses when there are 5 or more points.

outputsShown.output: Model used and number of data points.
Comparison of the personal slope with the baseline slope ("you gain more or less per hour than the baseline").

advancedComponent.expectedBaselineResult: Slope near 5 and intercept near 40, because that is the formula that generated the Kaggle data. Use this as a sanity check, not as a finding.
